effects.citation_sentence: Finally, we repeated the same set-up as Guo et al. used to show that VSTM1-v2 induced Th17 cell differentiation, by activating total CD4[+] T cells with anti-CD3, anti-CD28, and a Th17 polarizing cytokine mix [6].
effects.evidence: Results, final paragraph (Fig 1D): "The Th17 polarizing mix increased the percentage of IL-17[+] cells, but there was no effect of VSTM1-v2 (Fig 1D). effects.notes: Authors say they used the same set-up, polarizing mix and VSTM1-v2 concentrations as Guo, but they read out % intracellular IL-17+ cells after 10-12 days whereas Guo measured IL-17 release already at 72 h (Discussion notes this difference). That is a readout/timepoint change, so 'close experiment' is a plausible alternative; coded direct per the authors' 'repeated the same set-up' and the direct-vs-close tiebreaker. Small n (3 donors). Original author first names not given in the paper (initials only). Not coded: the neutrophil-dependence of DC-driven Th17 differentiation, which the authors say they 'confirmed' from their own prior work (Souwer et al., ref 8, 'Human TH17 cell development requires processing of dendritic cell-derived CXCL8 by neutrophil elastase') - here it functions as the positive control of the co-culture system, so it gets no row under 'controls are not claims'; a second coder might code it as a self-replication success (one candidate did).
